Wolanow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Wolanów, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Wolanów began soon after the town's founding in 1773, growing to 60% of the population by 1921 (313 residents). In July 1941 the Germans established a ghetto there, and by August 1942 its Jews - including many displaced from nearby Przytyk - were deported to Szydłowiec and then murdered at Treblinka. The cemetery's founding date is undocumented, though it likely postdates the town itself; it was fenced by the early 20th century. Under German orders, its tombstones were pulled up during the war to pave roads, and a 1952 survey recorded '90% of stones destroyed.' By 1985 the site had become a garbage dump. Today no fence, tombstones, or markers survive, and the cemetery's boundaries are no longer perceptible; it is currently owned by the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage.
